solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Corruptly petitions Conservative, relying on connections

indicators.note: something done corruptly is bent out of its proper shape, so the letters get twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A Tory politician is accused of crooked lobbying, getting things done through who he knows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouring relatives and friends, so a nepotistic system gets jobs and favours through personal ties rather than merit.

clue.text: Innocent person I put in cooler sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from the bottom upward, so backwards
put in means placed inside another word

parts.note: a fan cools you down
taken as written

explanation.surface: An innocent man is locked in the cooler, prison slang for a jail, and then sent up the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests a prison cell, but it is a device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: A naif is a naive or inexperienced person, someone innocent of the world's ways.

clue.text: Under pressure, pull in front of ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places one part beneath the other, so it comes after it

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
to row is to pull on oars

explanation.surface: Sailors under strain heave at the oars at the head of the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The prow is the pointed forward end of a ship's hull, the bow.

clue.text: Street food after meticulous starter

indicators.note: after places the food word behind the other word in the sequence
a starter comes first in a meal, so the painstaking word opens the answer

parts.note: meticulous means painstaking
fare is food and drink

explanation.surface: Street food served after a carefully made first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street food' reads as one phrase, but Street is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a main road or public way through a place, such as a street.

clue.text: French toast you pronounced in season

indicators.note: in means placed inside the seasoning word

parts.note: to season food is to salt it

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we want a letter that sounds like the word

parts.note: the letter U is said like this word

explanation.surface: A recipe for French toast that you season when you say so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French toast' looks like the eggy bread; it is a toast in French, the drinking salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Salut is the French word raised with glasses, like cheers, so it is a toast in French.

clue.text: Person setting up fashionable store, initially less creditworthy?

parts.note: in means in fashion

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that it follows

parts.note: the first letter of this word
a tall story is one hard to believe, so a taller one deserves less credit

explanation.surface: Someone setting up a trendy shop who has a weaker credit rating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creditworthy' suggests financial standing; here credit means belief, as in a tall tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An installer is someone who fits or sets up equipment.

clue.text: Adherent of far left or moderate movement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal short form for a Trotskyist
second meaning: a gait between walking and running, as a horse's

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is a radical left-winger or a member of a moderate political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate movement' reads as a centrist political group, but it is a medium-paced gait.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trot is slang for a follower of Trotsky, and a trot is a gait of medium speed.

clue.text: Salesperson responsible about carbon OK for making copies

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for responsible goes round the chemical symbol

parts.note: liable means legally answerable
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A sales rep in charge of carbon paper approves it for duplicating documents.
explanation.walkthrough: Carbon paper was once used to make copies, which ties the surface together.
explanation.definitionFit: Replicable means able to be reproduced or duplicated, so it is fit to be copied.

clue.text: Traveller's need boy mishandled — nothing is perfect

parts.note: a traveller needs a ticket

indicators.note: something mishandled is treated roughly and knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A traveller's luggage was mishandled by a porter, which goes to show nothing is perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: Tickety-boo is old-fashioned British slang for fine, in good order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickety-boo means everything is going smoothly and in order, an informal synonym for perfect or fine.

clue.text: Current company also reflected about name with ultimate critic of image

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the pair of words wraps around what follows

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the repeated word is read right to left

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company
N is the abbreviation for name
also means the company again: a second copy of the same abbreviation
ultimate means final

explanation.surface: An electrical firm's statement about naming, closing with a remark from an image critic — a jumble of business jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Also' tells you to repeat the company, and that second CO is the one turned round; the two CO pieces then sit either side of N, giving CO-N-OC.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast was literally a destroyer of religious images, and by extension is anyone who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions.

clue.text: Starts off every poem in collection in style of Homer

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first of each following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: An editor praises an anthology whose every poem opens in a grand Homeric manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer composed the Iliad and Odyssey, the archetypal long heroic poems, so his style is the epic style.

clue.text: Lying to wrong pro in dumb performance

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for the silent act

parts.note: miming is acting without words
a sin is a wrong
pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: Someone deceives a professional during a silent show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' looks like a professional; it is the Latin-derived 'for', as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: Misinforming means giving false information, which is what lying does.

clue.text: Was criterion changed? Just the opposite

indicators.note: something changed has been altered, so the letters of the question's first words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a standard was altered and gets the reply that the reverse happened.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes 'Was criterion changed?' look like a question being answered; it is all letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrariwise is an adverb meaning conversely or the other way round, the same as saying just the opposite.

clue.text: Denies CID's disrupted protest

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the detectives broke up a demonstration.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the plain-clothes detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissidence is open disagreement with authority, a form of protest.

clue.text: Doctor deals with livid rash

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor treats an angry red skin eruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' and 'rash' paint a medical scene, but rash is the adjective for reckless and Doctor is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash decision is hasty and unwise, which is what ill-advised means.

clue.text: Serving American in pub one litre at first is not reasonable

indicators.note: in tells us the serviceman is placed inside the drinking establishment
at first says these pieces come at the front, ahead of everything else

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for litre
a local is the pub nearest your home
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier ordering a full litre in a pub is told this is unreasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's regular neighbourhood pub; GI is placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical defies sound reasoning, so it is not reasonable.

clue.text: Crop harvested in island, sign of winter's arrival

indicators.note: the crop gathered in from the island follows it, so the two are set side by side

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
corn is a harvested crop

explanation.surface: Grain gathered on an island signals that winter is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun enters this zodiac sign around 22 December, the winter solstice.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricorn is the star sign whose period begins at the winter solstice, so it marks winter's start.

clue.text: Country in which I do some computing with single line

indicators.note: with a single line means one of the doubled line letters is dropped, leaving just one

parts.note: taken as written
to tally is to count up

explanation.surface: Someone describes a country where they do some computing work on a single phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: TALLY has two Ls, each L standing for line; keeping a single one leaves TALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a nation in southern Europe.

clue.text: Notes are set out along such lines for workforce

definitions.text: Notes are set out along such lines
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the five horizontal lines on which music is written
second meaning: the employees of an organisation

explanation.surface: Memos are sent along certain lines to the employees of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like office memos; it means musical notes, written on the five lines of a stave.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical stave is also called a staff, and the people employed by an organisation are its staff.

clue.text: Wine following stew, something artistically put together

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
F is the abbreviation for following
an olio is a spicy stew of meat and vegetables

explanation.surface: Wine served after a stew makes an artful combination at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a collection of an artist's work assembled to show their range.

clue.text: Personal writing, including edition that's strategically misleading

indicators.note: including means taking something inside, so one word holds the other within it

parts.note: a diary is a private daily record
an edition is one version of a text

explanation.surface: A published edition of someone's private journal turns out to be deliberately deceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A diversionary move draws attention away from the real aim, a tactic meant to mislead.

clue.text: Deliver article to top or bottom level

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending letters to the top means writing them upward, so backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver from something
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A courier is told to take a parcel to the top floor or the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs top with bottom; only 'bottom level' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, literally the point directly beneath an observer.

clue.text: Hide son with relatives

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A boy is hidden away with his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' reads as a verb, but it is the noun for an animal's pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, especially when tanned.

clue.text: Undertaking to form union with Liberal hero

parts.note: the vow 'I do' is spoken to enter marriage
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal party hero pledges to form a political alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone greatly admired, a hero figure.

clue.text: Curious and boisterous? Not I

indicators.note: not I says one letter, the I, must be left out of the word

parts.note: boisterous means loud

explanation.surface: Someone is asked whether they are inquisitive and rowdy, and denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious in the sense of inquisitive about others' business, the meaning of nosy.

clue.text: Deceived both good and wicked, each needing change of character

indicators.note: a change of character means one letter in each word is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Saints and sinners alike were taken in, and both need to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: The G of good becomes H and the C of wicked becomes N; 'change of character' sounds like moral reform but means one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoodwink is to trick or fool someone, so hoodwinked means deceived.

clue.text: Top journo introducing conclusions of odd survey that shows current circulation

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in ahead, so the journalist comes first and the rest follows

parts.note: the editor is the top journalist on a paper

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so only the final letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the final letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A senior journalist launches a strange survey to show a newspaper's present readership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current circulation' looks like a newspaper's sales figures, fitting the journalist; it is water going round.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air moving round against the main flow, a circular current.

clue.text: Multinational group set trap in foreign currency derivative

parts.note: UNO is the United Nations Organization

indicators.note: set means placed, so the trap is put into the currency
in shows where the trap goes: inside the money word

parts.note: the rial is the currency of Iran and other countries
a gin is a snare for catching animals

explanation.surface: An international body lays a trap involving a financial derivative in a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derivative' looks like a financial instrument fitting the currency, but it is the adjective meaning copied.
explanation.definitionFit: Derivative work borrows from others rather than being original, so it is unoriginal.
